subject: MAP & pilot acceptance — usage definition, true-up, and price-protection details
messages:
From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
To: Jared Liu <jared.liu@finwell.tech>
Cc: procurement@finwell.tech
Date: Wed, 20 May 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: MAP & pilot acceptance — usage definition, true-up, and price-protection details

Hi Jared —

Thanks for the time yesterday. Per our discussion I’m attaching an initial MAP and SOW draft for the pilot phase. High level proposal below so we have one canonical place to debate acceptance criteria and commercial mechanics: 

- Pilot window: 6 weeks (start: provisioned env + test dataset ingestion)
- Pilot acceptance: mutually agreed evaluation set (accuracy + stability) and 7 consecutive days with average 95th pctl latency < 350ms under the agreed QPS profile
- Commit ramp: if pilot accepted, customer commits to a staged monthly commit: 100k tokens month 1 -> 500k month 3 -> 1.5M month 6, with a 12-month pricing schedule
- Discounting: tiered volume discount after commit thresholds; pilot discount applies only to committed tokens during pilot month
- True-up: quarterly true-up for any consumption above committed tokens; proposal is pro-rata true-up applied at the end of the quarter with an overage rate that steps down as commit tiers are reached
- Price protection: hold committed price for 12 months from contract signature; non-committed pay-as-you-go may see pricing adjustments with 30-day notice

A few technical/commercial clarifications we need from you to finalize redlines:
1) What should count as "billable usage" for the pilot and true-ups? (input tokens, output tokens, system/prompts, or some combination)
2) For acceptance, are the latency/throughput metrics above acceptable or do you prefer a different metric set?
3) Procurement: preferred PO/contract cadence and any internal approvals we should plan for?

Attachments: MAP-draft-v1.pdf, SOW-draft.docx

Proposed next steps: if you can confirm (1)-(3) this week, we’ll produce a redline-ready agreement and a clean price table to embed in the SOW.

Best,
Monica
Monica Patel | Enterprise Sales | Redwood Inference
monica.patel@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0192

---
Note: SOW assumes "billable usage" = input + output tokens processed via Redwood API unless otherwise defined in the contract.

From: Jared Liu <jared.liu@finwell.tech>
To: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@finwell.tech
Date: Wed, 20 May 2026 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: MAP & pilot acceptance — usage definition, true-up, and price-protection details

Monica —

Thanks for the clear outline and the docs. A couple quick clarifications from our side before we loop legal: 

- Acceptance: the throughput/latency targets look reasonable. Can we add an availability SLA during the 7-day acceptance window (e.g., 99% availability of the provisioned endpoint)?
- Billable usage: Finwell's procurement team typically expects "billable usage" to exclude system telemetry, health-check pings, and developer sandbox activity. We prefer billable = user-facing input + output tokens for the evaluation, but need Redwood to confirm how that maps to API-level counters and logs.
- True-up: if we exceed committed tokens mid-quarter due to an unexpected ramp, how do you calculate the overage? Is it billed immediately or netted at quarter-end? We typically prefer end-of-quarter netting.

Attaching our evaluation criteria workbook for visibility. Procurement is on cc to coordinate PO timing.

Cheers,
Jared
Jared Liu | Head of Platform Engineering | Finwell Technologies
jared.liu@finwell.tech
Attachment: Finwell-eval-criteria.xlsx

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 20 May 2026 16:30:00 -0700
Subject: Internal: proposed redline positions for Finwell MAP/SOW

Team —

Quick internal note before we send the formal redline: below are the positions I recommend we hold to keep economics protected while being flexible for a new strategic customer.

1) Billable usage definition: define as "billable tokens = sum of input tokens and generated (output) tokens processed by the Redwood API for production and approved test datasets." Explicitly exclude health-check pings, developer sandbox requests, and logs used solely for telemetry/analytics. This gives us clarity for true-up calculations.

2) True-up mechanics: quarterly reconciliation. Any consumption above the quarterly committed tokens is billed at the overage rate for the tier in effect for that quarter. If the customer subsequently secures a higher commit tier within the same contract year, we will apply a retroactive credit for the prior quarter equal to the difference between the overage paid and the contract tier price (i.e., waterfall credit, capped at the amount of the prior overage).

3) Price protection: hold committed unit price for 12 months from signature for committed tokens. PAYG rates for non-committed usage may be adjusted with 30 days' notice; immediate changes cannot be applied to prior invoices.

4) Acceptance criteria: keep the mutually-agreed eval set + 7-day stability window. Add a 99% availability target during the acceptance window as requested by the customer.

5) PO & billing: accept Net 30 by default; where the customer requests extended terms, require finance signoff and an approved credit memo process.

I’ve attached an internal guidance note with suggested clause language: redline-guidance-internal.md. If Monica agrees, I’ll convert these positions into clause-level redlines and circulate a tracked PDF.

-Laura
Laura Bennett | Director, Commercial Contracts | Redwood Inference

From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
To: Jared Liu <jared.liu@finwell.tech>
Cc: procurement@finwell.tech, laura.bennett@redwood.com, rishi.malhotra@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 21 May 2026 09:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: MAP & pilot acceptance — usage definition, true-up, and price-protection details

Jared / procurement —

Thanks for the quick responses and the workbook, Jared. Based on your feedback we’ve updated our positions and proposed specific clause language below (happy to send a redline PDF once you confirm):

Proposed MAP highlights (summary):
- Pilot: 6 weeks (provisioning + ingestion week, 4 weeks evaluation, 1 week stability)
- Acceptance metrics: mutually agreed evaluation set (accuracy thresholds) + 7 consecutive days with 95th pctl latency < 350ms and 99% availability during the stability window
- Billable usage: defined as user-facing input tokens + generated output tokens processed through the Redwood inference API. System telemetry, health-checks, and developer sandbox traffic explicitly excluded. Contract will reference the API usage counters as the source of truth for reconciliation.
- True-up: quarterly reconciliation (end-of-quarter netting). Any overage is billed at the applicable overage rate; if customer upgrades to a higher committed tier within the contract year, we’ll issue a retroactive credit for prior overages based on the new tier pricing (waterfall credit).
- Price protection: committed unit price locked for 12 months from signature for committed tokens. PAYG rates are subject to change with 30 days' notice and will not apply retroactively to invoices already issued.

Next steps: 
1) If this summary matches Finwell's expectations, we’ll produce a tracked-change redline for the SOW and contract by EOD Friday.
2) Procurement: please confirm PO/PO approval timeline — Laura indicated Net 30 as standard; if you need alternate terms, flag now so Finance can review.
3) Legal: if you have specific contract templates or must-haves, please share so our GC can align.

If helpful we can schedule a 30-minute call to walk the clauses live. Let me know what works.

Best,
Monica
Monica Patel | Enterprise Sales | Redwood Inference
monica.patel@redwood.com
